title: 1.2 Billion People Use AI Every Week. Almost None Own It.
scaffold_note: Decision scaffold for the FROM-SCRATCH rebuild of soa-01, opened 2026-10-26 (JOB REBUILD-SOA01-1) under the owner's rebuild order of the same day. This branch starts empty; nothing from the first draft (the old build, branch video/soa-01) is copied as settled. The first draft is evidence: a field may adopt a value the first draft carried ONLY when this branch records its own reasoning for it. A field this phase does not decide ships OPEN with an empty rationale and a named route.

objective.value: Show 1.2 billion weekly users rent AI access while owning none of the layer around it.
objective.rationale: The piece exists to make one number testify about ownership. The first draft's catalogue objective (16 words, recorded as GROUNDED in its script record) survives re-derivation unchanged: the fact it names (1.2B weekly users) is still the lane's load-bearing fact, and the rent/own gap is still the Academy's prescription read against it. Adopted because the reasoning re-checks out in this branch, not because the first draft carried it.

objective.record: files/short-soa01-billion-script.md — 'Objective (catalogue, GROUNDED, 16 words)'; canon.md §1–2 (the harness is where ownership lives)

message.value: Adoption is total. Ownership is zero. (Viewer restatement: 'Over a billion people now use AI every week — through a chat box they rent, keeping nothing of the layer around it.')
message.rationale: One message, two clauses: the scale of adoption and the absence of ownership, stated as a pair so the viewer can hold both in one breath. The essence line is the piece's own closing line (L6) — the message and the payoff are the same sentence, which is what makes the short quotable. The viewer restatement is kept because it translates the essence into the viewer's own situation (a chat box THEY rent).
message.source: archer reasoning (this branch, 2026-10-26), from the first draft's script record (essence + viewer restatement, 2026-10-22)

audience.value: The renters themselves: people who use AI every week through a chat box they do not own — the very users the 1.2B statistic counts. Secondarily, the AI-curious public who read adoption numbers as good news and have never asked who owns the layer. The misconception the piece corrects: 'I use ChatGPT every week, so the AI setup is mine — my instructions, my memory, my files belong to me.' In fact all of it lives on the provider's terms and vanishes when the tab closes.
audience.rationale: Decided by reasoning from the piece's own evidence, since the first draft's record never named an audience (its board phase-0 check stood pending — the one open scaffold field the first draft carried to its end). The evidence: (1) the closing bridge card speaks to the renter in the second person — 'Renters can become owners.' — a conversion appeal that only makes sense addressed to renters; (2) L5 explains the gap 'in doctrine language a newcomer can hold' (script record's own words), i.e. addressed to someone inside the chat box, not to builders; (3) the lane's phase-0 studies write for the general public encountering an adoption statistic (SOA-02's Pew brief addresses U.S. adults at large); (4) the funnel design — bridge to the Toaster long-form — presumes a viewer who rents today and could own tomorrow. Confidence: reasoning-grade, not measurement-grade; the residual is named in decisions/randomness-register.md.
